name: Bookly
category: an AI reading companion for busy professionals

headline: Read less.
Remember more.
idea.promise: Bookly turns the books you mean to read into ten-minute conversations you actually finish. The brand should feel like a good library: calm, warm, a little bookish, and never in a hurry.
idea.personality: Warm, clear, quietly clever, never smug.

pillars.title: Calm over clever
pillars.body: Lots of space, soft paper tones and one deep green. Nothing blinks, nothing shouts.

pillars.title: Books first
pillars.body: Real covers, real quotes, real page numbers. The product is about reading, so the brand looks like reading.

pillars.title: One serif, one sans
pillars.body: Fraunces for headlines gives the bookish warmth. Inter does all the work everywhere else.

pillars.title: Plain words
pillars.body: We explain like a well-read friend, not a productivity guru.

dark.name: Forest
dark.use: Dark sections, the app's night mode, social posts.

accent.name: Bookly green
accent.use: The one action per view, links, highlights.

support.name: Bookmark
support.use: Small highlights only: a ribbon, a streak badge. Never text on linen.

headline: Like a friend
who reads a lot.
voice.summary: We sound like a well-read friend: warm, specific, a little playful, never preachy about productivity.
write: Finish the book you started in March.
Ten minutes a day. One chapter at a time.
We read the boring bits so you don't have to.
not: Unlock 10x knowledge with AI-powered reading hacks 🚀
The ultimate productivity tool for high performers.
voice.names: Bookly in text, bookly (lowercase) in the logo, Bookly Inc. for legal.

headline: Real books,
real light.
imagery.summary: Real books, real hands, real reading corners. Warm daylight, linen and wood. Never stock 'success' photos or glowing brains.
do: Books on tables, in hands, on trains.
Close crops of pages and margins.
dont: Stacks of money, trophies, mountain summits.
imagery.style: Documentary photograph, calm and unhurried. Warm daylight from a window, linen, paper and wood tones, a little deep green, muted colour, soft contrast, shallow depth of field, 50mm lens, fine film grain. Leave quiet space on one side for a headline.
imagery.avoid: text, letters, logos, watermarks, readable book titles or screens, robots, glowing brains, neon, gradients, 3D renders, stacks of money, trophies, mountain summits, posed stock smiles, extra fingers

prompts.title: Reading corner
prompts.subject: A person in their thirties reading a paperback in a deep armchair by a window, legs tucked up, a mug of tea on the side table, late afternoon light

prompts.title: Commute chapter
prompts.use: Social posts about reading in ten minutes
prompts.subject: A commuter reading a phone held low on a quiet morning train, a paperback poking out of their bag, soft light through the window, other passengers blurred

prompts.title: Margins
prompts.subject: Close-up of an open book with pencil underlines and a small handwritten note in the margin, a green ribbon bookmark across the page

prompts.title: The shelf
prompts.subject: A wooden bookshelf at home with books lying at different angles, a small plant, a reading lamp switched on, most of the frame calm and uncluttered

prompts.title: Bedside
prompts.use: Story backgrounds with text on top
prompts.subject: A bedside table at night with a closed book, reading glasses and a small warm lamp, the rest of the room in soft darkness

prompts.title: Desk notes
prompts.use: Blog headers about remembering what you read
prompts.subject: Top-down view of a linen-covered desk with an open notebook of short handwritten summaries, a pen and a cup of coffee, generous empty space

after: Keep the natural grade: warm, muted, no filters or heavy presets.
Check hands, faces and pages at 100%. Reject warped fingers, fake lettering and plastic skin.
Crop so the subject sits on one third and the quiet space holds the headline.
rules: Generated images are for mood, backgrounds and editorial scenes.
Never present a generated person as a real customer, author, team member or testimonial.
Never generate the logo, real book covers or app screens. Add those afterwards in the layout.
